transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

This is most often a blocked defrost drain: defrost water cannot reach the tray at the back, so it overflows under the salad drawers. Switch the fridge off and unplug it, remove the drawers and put towels down. Find the small hole/channel at the bottom of the inside back wall, then gently flush it with a little warm water using a squeezy bottle or turkey baster; a soft pipe cleaner can loosen debris, but do not use wire or anything sharp. If it is frozen over, let it thaw fully first. If water still returns after the drain runs freely, the next likely causes are excess condensation from a dirty/gapped door seal or, if it has a water dispenser/ice maker, a leaking water line.

ok thanks, il have a look. theres a little groove and a hole at the bottom of the back wall, its got bits of lettuce and gunk in it. is it ok to clear it with a cotton bud and warm water? the water is only inside the fridge not near the plug btw

Yes — a cotton bud is fine for lifting out the loose lettuce and gunk, provided you are gentle and do not push it deeply into the hole. With the fridge switched off and unplugged, remove what you can, then use a small amount of warm (not boiling) water to flush the hole; a squeezy bottle is better than pouring. Stop if the bud snags or the water will not drain — do not use wire, a skewer or anything sharp, as the drain channel can be damaged. That visible debris makes a blocked defrost drain the clear leading cause of the water under the drawers. After clearing it, does a little warm water run away through the hole rather than sit in the groove?
ok i did it with a cotton bud and warm water and the water went straight down the hole. no more pooling over the next few days so looks like its sorted. should i do anything else?

No further repair should be needed — clearing the blocked defrost drain has resolved it. Just wipe the groove and drain area out periodically, and try to keep loose food or packaging from sitting against the back wall so debris cannot wash into the hole. If water returns despite the drain remaining clear, then check the door seal and that the fridge is sitting slightly level or very slightly tilted back; otherwise, it sounds sorted. Is there anything else with the fridge-freezer you would like help with?
